title.en: A shirt designed in one country, made in another

text.en: The phone in your hand may have parts from many countries. Globalisation is the growing connection between economies through trade and investment.

Multinational corporations (MNCs) own or control production in more than one country. They set up offices and factories where costs are low and markets large.
MNCs spread production through foreign investment, joint ventures and by placing orders with small producers.
Foreign trade connects markets in different countries. It gives producers and consumers more choices and can bring prices closer.
Technology, such as telecommunication and the internet, has made globalisation faster.
In 1991 India adopted liberalisation: removing trade barriers and controls, and reforms in industries and foreign investment.
The World Trade Organisation (WTO) sets rules for international trade, but critics say rich countries have more power.
Special Economic Zones (SEZs) were set up with world-class facilities and tax holidays to attract foreign companies.
The impact is unequal: consumers and some producers gained, but small producers and workers faced pressure. A fair globalisation would give opportunities to all.

problem.en: India's exports are Rs 70 and imports Rs 50 (in crore). What is the trade surplus?

why.en: A positive result is a surplus.

prompt.en: Discuss how globalisation affects small producers.

requiredIdeas.en: Need for support and fair rules

points.en: MNCs produce in more than one country.
WTO and SEZs shape trade and investment.
